s2.p1: Chad has **no member** in the World DanceSport Federation. Its stages belong to traditional and contemporary dance.
s2.p2: In 2018, N’Djamena’s **Souar Souar** dance festival held its 7th edition. Its name means ==“Come, come and dance together!”==

s3.p: were performed at Place de la Nation in N’Djamena on **11 August 2026**, for the 66th anniversary of Chad’s independence.

s4.p1: A young man with a **paralysed leg** is admired on N’Djamena’s dance floors. It was inspired by real dancer **Souleymane Démé**.
s4.p2: Mahamat-Saleh Haroun’s film competed for the ==Palme d’Or==, and won the Vulcan prize for its cinematography.

s5.name: SAÏ
s5.p: A **collective dance** where men and women dance together, presented as a symbol of unity and social cohesion.

s5.name: RICHAT
s5.p: The **fan dance** of eastern Chad. It was historically reserved for **royal circles**.

s6.p: At the **Gerewol**, Wodaabe men paint their faces and dance in lines, rolling their eyes and flashing their teeth. **Women** pick the winners with a tap.

s7.p: A Massa retreat where boys and men learn **wrestling, music and dance** with their cattle becomes Chad’s **first** UNESCO intangible heritage, shared with Cameroon.
s7.p2: All **23 provinces** brought their dances to N’Djamena for 16 days. Mayo-Kebbi Est danced the Guruna on 3 January 2026.
